headline: Reykjavík City and the Blue Lagoon were also attacked on Nov 25, but nothing public links those attacks to 1984 Hosting.
summary: Added c010 (Reported) on sources s006 (Vísir, Nov 26, quoting a CERT-IS official) and s007 (RÚV, Nov 26), timeline row t006 and question q008, answered Not established. Vísir reports the Nov 25 attacks on Reykjavík City's systems and the Blue Lagoon; the CERT-IS official could not be sure even those two were related, and RÚV says the Reykjavík attackers used Microsoft Azure. Neither outlet links them to 1984. Re-read the status page (s001) in a browser at 2:08 PM ET: last updated 18:22 UTC, wording unchanged, websites still not back before the expected 21:00 UTC return, virtual servers still being restored; service stays partly-back (c006, last_checked moved). CERT-IS's news list has nothing naming 1984. Supplier question (q007) still open: 1984 has named no customers, no organisation has said it was affected or that it uses 1984, and 1984's own sites did not load. Theory sweep: Hacker News threads 50656686 and 50579592 read whole; nothing raised by several commenters beyond what q003 to q005 already cover; Reddit not read (refused). Not eligible for resolved: services are partly back.
author: Research agent

headline: 1984 Hosting says a targeted cyberattack got into its systems; email is back and websites are due back from 21:00 UTC on Nov 26.
summary: New incident page. 1984 Hosting's status page (s001) says unauthorised activity followed a targeted cyberattack, services were suspended, and customer data was untouched except on seven websites that were the original target; email is back, websites expected from 21:00 UTC Nov 26, VPS restoration ongoing. DV (s002) carries the Nov 20 joint statement with CERT-IS; Vísir (s003) quotes the managing director on pro-Palestine sites and a likely nation-state. CERT-IS notices (s004, s005) on the Nov 25 national response plan do not name 1984. Main answer Confirmed on the company's own word, filed under hack-stated; incident_type attack; service partly-back on c006. Size Local. Theory sweep: Hacker News threads read (one with a single comment, one with four); theories recorded as q003 to q005. Privacy check done: the status page's contact address is covered in the screenshot; the managing director is named by role only.
author: Research agent
